items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: I think Harry Belafonte has made a, uh, Blackberry song.

ctx.x: around New Orleans? Well, there were, there were, uh, I won't say that, uh, that there were street singers that merely sang, but there were, there were, uh, vendors who had a street song. They would sing now and then. I remember mostly blackberries, an old Negro woman that used to come around the neighborhood where we lived, and she used to blackberries there. I remember that, uh, somebody was, uh, trying to, to call to my sister one time. My sister was back in the house, and, uh, the neighbor wanted, had called…

Oh, in, uh, the twenties, Paramount issued a record of street cries, which was a little strange, a folklore that you might not think they'd recognize them. But then, um, in recent years, a, uh, I think Harry Belafonte has made a, uh, Blackberry song. Well, there used to be any number

of different vendors going around them. There was the man that cleaned out the chimney, you know. Oh, yeah. They'd always wear them always wear them a plug hat along the outfit. I don't know why them chimney sweeps would have a plug hat, and they had a call. There's a story about the peanut bender song coming from an authentic peanut bender.
